title: The Memory Garden
question: One beautiful moment of music that made you feel you belonged.

seeds.text: It was a really beautiful first time for me to be part of the Open Source Orchestra in real time, and shout out to Alaska for the invite to Mumbai, and it was a beautiful experience.
The first time we ever sang together was in Amsterdam after Devconnect was happening, just in the lobby.

seeds.text: But this Open Source Orchestra brought everyone together.
seeds.context: it really was the highlight of Devconnect

seeds.text: So, we go there and really have a great time, because, honestly, Devcon 8, we really were the heartbeat of Devcon 8, really were the heartbeat.
We made a song in real time featuring the one and only Ben on vocals and Shaka on ukulele.
seeds.source: words lane · verified verbatim against the public transcript

seeds.text: Levi and Alaska on the sax and Ben singing his heart out. And then there's someone on the piano for the first time.
seeds.source: words lane · verified verbatim against the public transcript

seeds.text: So during the hackathon, we had a small setup over there in which, like, whenever we used to get frustrated from coding at night, we used to go on the stage and we start – we used to start playing. And Shaka joined us and we started playing some Bollywood songs and jammed together. That was the point when I thought, okay, like, this is a new space.
seeds.place: ETHMumbai · the hackathon stage at night

seeds.text: Like, we have seen open-source – open-source softwares, but this was something new for me where anyone can come and play together and we can have multiple global cultures coming together and, you know, making a single music out of it so which everyone can connect.

So, and I had no idea that I would be able to, like, you know, sing or do anything. Like, it was so, like, just love what you guys are doing and what you've done. And, yeah, and I'm just, like, so, you know, grateful that I was able to, you know, be part of it.
Young college students who've never sang in a space like that, getting to sing in the Jio World Centre.

seeds.text: We learned a lot of stuff from Aniket that how Indian classical music works and you can play a sitar on a guitar.
seeds.source: words lane · verified verbatim against the public transcript

seeds.text: This stage brought me back to my nostalgic school choir time where we used to sing hymns.
seeds.source: words lane · verified verbatim against the public transcript

seeds.text: [ETH] London 2019, that was my first event … I couldn't believe 10,000 people could fit into one environment.
seeds.source: words lane · verified verbatim against the public transcript

seeds.text: We made Devcon music space a sanctuary, not a stage.
seeds.source: words lane · verified verbatim against the public transcript

seeds.text: People think it's really cool to come together all over the world and play music together. That'd be the dream.
seeds.source: words lane · verified verbatim against the public transcript

seeds.text: The golden thread I hear is that music lets everyone belong: no auditions, just listening first and making room.
